chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Abu Basir, he said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The quarrelers are ruined, and the Muslims are saved. Verily, the Muslims are the noble ones.

key_terms.أَصْحَابُ الْكَلَامِ: People of speech/theology, referring to those engaged in speculative debate about divine attributes
key_terms.النُّجَبَاءُ: The noble ones, a term for the elite or distinguished believers

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the ruined 'people of speech' and the saved Muslims according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In al-Tawhid, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) warning that the 'people of speech' (ahl al-kalam)—those who rely on speculative reasoning rather than divine revelation—face ruin, while the general Muslim community (al-nujaba) attains salvation. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on preserving simple, authentic faith against the complexities of Kalam theology, distinguishing the true believers as the 'noble ones' who remain steadfast in their core beliefs.
